result.topic_en: Euler reduces the variational solution for a space curve with a maximum/minimum property to two second-order differential equations, divides one by the other, and integrates to obtain the relation z - qx = n(y - px).
result.transcription:
Ex quibus solutionem nostri problematis elici oportet, id quod plurimam solertiam atque insignia calculi artificia postulat.

24. Cum sit $\partial.\frac{pv}{s} = \frac{v\partial p}{s} + p.\partial.\frac{v}{s}$ et $\partial.\frac{qv}{s} = \frac{v\partial q}{s} + q.\partial.\frac{v}{s}$, ob $\partial.\frac{v}{s} = \frac{sx\partial x}{-v}$, facta hac substitutione solutio perducetur ad has duas aequationes:
I. $(y\partial x - x\partial y) = \frac{v^2\partial p}{ss}$,
II. $(z\partial x - x\partial z) = \frac{vv\partial q}{ss}$;
quamobrem videamus, quibusnam artificiis hinc formulas integrabiles elicere queamus, quandoquidem hae aequationes manifesto sunt differentiales secundi gradus, ob $p = \frac{\partial y}{\partial x}$ et $q = \frac{\partial z}{\partial x}$.

25. Harum aequationum altera per alteram divisa praebet $\frac{y\partial x - x\partial y}{z\partial x - x\partial z} = \frac{\partial p}{\partial q}$, unde nascitur haec aequatio:
$\frac{\partial p}{y\partial x - x\partial y} = \frac{\partial q}{z\partial x - x\partial z}$, sive $\frac{\partial p}{y - px} = \frac{\partial q}{z - qx}$.
Quodsi jam haec aequatio ita referatur: $-\frac{x\partial p}{y - px} = \frac{x\partial q}{z - qx}$, facile patet in utraque fractione numeratorem esse ipsum differentiale denominatoris, ideoque fore:
$l\,\overline{y - px} = l\,\overline{z - qx} - ln$,
unde habebimus $z - qx = n(y - px)$, ita ut hinc jam determinetur $z$ per reliquas litteras.
